IMPLEMENT STORY #448: #344 follow-ups: decision 0029's addendum matches what shipped, and the view offers only commands the engine accepts

You are implementing exactly one story from the code-health epic (#330) on branch story-448-344-follow-ups, already checked out in this worktree off origin/main. The issue text below is the whole framing: its "What is asked" and "Acceptance" sections are what done means. Decision 0071 (the architectural principles) is ACCEPTED, and the house rules' Architecture section states its Rust form. Build to it. Where the issue leaves a choice to the operator, implement the option it recommends (or the first listed), keep it small, and say which you took in your result notes so the pull request can ask for the ruling. If the story is too large for one reviewable commit, deliver the smallest complete slice that meets acceptance items end to end, and name the rest in notes as follow-ups. Do not deliver a half-built everything.

RULES
- Scope: this story and nothing beside it. Follow-ups go in your notes, not in the diff. Prefer targeted edits over rewrites. A structural move keeps behaviour and bytes: every existing test keeps its name and its assertions unless the story says otherwise.
- A gate must be shown to bite: for every new check, plant the violation it exists to refuse, run the check and see it fail with the stated reason, then remove the plant. Record each removal control (what you planted, the command, the failure text) in your notes and in the commit message.
- Tests: assert exact values and exact error text, never is_err() alone. A new gate fails closed: read typed data where it exists; where you must scan text, refuse what the scanner does not recognise.
- Coverage: the repository enforces literal 100% line, branch and function coverage (scripts/coverage-exact.sh), which the controller runs after you; do not run that script. Keep every new production line and branch reachable by a test, and delete code you make unreachable.
- Frozen surfaces do not move: contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/. Decisions 0001 and 0003 stand. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063): add no Windows code.
- Every witness digest your change moves is re-pinned from the tests' own reported values, never computed by hand.
- Main requires twelve status checks; keep their names: "delivered by brokkr", "MSRV (1.88)", "format, clippy, contracts", "test (ubuntu-latest)", "test (macos-latest)", "exact coverage gate", "dependency licenses (cargo-deny)", "non-Rust lints", "baseline ratchets", "RustSec dependency audit", "release binary artifact", "mutants in the diff: brokkr-core". Three of them bite code moves:
  - baseline ratchets (quality/ratchet.sh, quality/README.md): lines per file at most max(baseline, 800) production and max(baseline, 2000) test; no new jscpd clone (50 tokens, 5 lines) in production, test or data. A repeated block needs a helper, not a copy. A function or file that is MOVED counts as new, so name any raised baseline in your notes for the PR's Ruling: line.
  - #337's suppressions: every suppression is #[expect(lint, reason = "...")], never #[allow]; quality/suppressions.txt must equal the tree. After adding or removing one, regenerate it with BROKKR_REGENERATE_SUPPRESSIONS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test suppressions, and remove an #[expect] your change leaves unfulfilled (clippy reports it). A shrink needs no ruling; a new suppression does.
  - mutants in the diff: brokkr-core: a brokkr-core change must not add a mutant no test catches (quality/mutants/brokkr-core.missed.txt is empty).
- Gates before you report complete, all clean, run from the worktree root:
  - cargo fmt --all -- --check
  - cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
  - cargo test -p <crate> for every crate you touched, and cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test suppressions
  - typos --hidden
  - quality/ratchet.sh files, and quality/ratchet.sh clones
  - shellcheck -S warning <each .sh you changed>, and actionlint if you touched .github/
  - git diff --check
- Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job or a scheduled wake-up pending: this seat is non-interactive, so ending the turn ends the process and your result file is never written.
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#448)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed. Anything you did not observe is pending, not done.

HOST FACTS AND PARALLEL WORK

- Main is c59e8e8b (2026-09-27). Track B has merged, the merge queue included (#451), and so have #352 (one transcript path) and #344 (operator commands as one module, engine/operator.rs). Main lands only through the merge queue.
- Operator ruling, 2026-09-26, the threat model for every gate: catch realistic ACCIDENTAL misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read. A deliberate, exotic evasion is a LOW residual.
- Host tool versions, as ci.yml pins them: typos 1.50.2, shellcheck 0.11.0, zizmor 1.30.1, actionlint 1.7.12, lychee (setup-lychee's digest), jscpd 5.3.2, cargo-shear 1.14.0, cargo-crap 0.5.0, cargo-public-api 0.52.0, cargo-mutants 27.1.0, stable Rust 1.98.0 (rust-toolchain.toml), MSRV 1.88.0. CI runs actionlint with SHELLCHECK_OPTS='-S warning'; run it the same way.
- On this host typos, shellcheck, actionlint, zizmor and lychee live in ~/.local/bin, and jscpd, cargo-shear and cargo-crap in ~/.cargo/bin. In CI they are installed by the pinned install-action and setup-* actions.
- Other stories are implemented in parallel on other branches. Stay out of their files unless your story needs them, and say so in notes if it does:
  - #356 (Windows removal): cfg(windows) code across crates, crates/brokkr-cli/tests/hosts.rs, docs and specs.
  - #448 and #354 fire together: #448 touches docs/decisions/0029 and brokkr-view's operator_commands plus Muninn; #354 touches brokkr-store, core fold (apply / fold_onto) and the engine's append path.
  - Later, one at a time: #356 (Windows removal), #355 (retire unused), #354 (journal hot path) and #352 (one transcript path).
- This story follows #344 (PR #446), which moved the operator verbs to crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/operator.rs and added brokkr_core::fold::{OperatorCommand, Refusal, acceptance_refusal}. Its landing named both items of this issue as lows.
- Item 1 is prose in docs/decisions/0029-fenced-append.md's 2026-09-27 addendum. Correct it to the shipped behaviour, and do not change code to match it. In the addendum's own words, the operator ruled the refusal word and the typed API. Keep that sentence, and correct only what it lists as public. Check the lists against quality/public-api/brokkr-core.txt and brokkr-runtime.txt.
- Item 2: brokkr_view::operator_commands and Muninn's dossier (crates/brokkr-cli/src/muninn.rs). brokkr-view is pure: it may depend on brokkr-core, where acceptance_refusal lives, and on nothing that does I/O (#336's purity gate). Prefer calling acceptance_refusal over restating it.

THE ISSUE (#448), verbatim:

Part of epic #330, track C. Follow-ups from #344 (PR #446), both rated low by its landing, `landing-pr-for-story-344-operato-35620f97`.

1. **Decision 0029's 2026-09-27 addendum misstates what shipped.**
   - It says a retry on a run parked before any phase is refused "before any append". Both doors, `operator_command_racing` and `apply_fenced_racing` in `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/operator.rs`, journal `operator/commanded` and then `operator/rejected` with `no_phase_to_retry`. Only the acceptance is never written.
   - It puts `Head` on brokkr-core's public surface. `Head` is a private struct in brokkr-runtime's `engine/operator.rs`. The public additions are `OperatorCommand`, `Refusal` and `acceptance_refusal` in brokkr-core, and `CommandWord` and `FencedCommand` in brokkr-runtime.

   **Ask:** correct the text to the shipped, tested behaviour, and do not change the code to match the text. Refusing before the command is journaled would drop evidence, and exporting `Head` would add a public item with no consumer (decision 0071 ruling 6). The operator confirms the corrected wording on the PR.
2. **brokkr-view states the admission rule a second time** (decision 0071 ruling 5). `brokkr_view::operator_commands` (`crates/brokkr-view/src/lib.rs`, around line 699) decides the offered commands from the status string alone. For a run parked by `SELECT-NO-DEFAULT` before any `phase/entered`, it offers `[retry, stop]`, and the Muninn dossier (`crates/brokkr-cli/src/muninn.rs`, around line 297) prints that beside `phase: null`. The engine refuses that retry with `no_phase_to_retry`.

   **Ask:** derive the offered commands from the `RunState`, keeping each `OperatorCommand` for which `brokkr_core::fold::acceptance_refusal` returns `None`. Pin the phase-`None` park with a test bound by a mutation.

## Acceptance

- The addendum's two sentences match `operator.rs` and the public-API snapshots.
- A run parked before any phase offers only `stop` in the view and in Muninn's dossier, and a test fails if `retry` comes back.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.


result.notes:
Story #448, one signed-off commit 44dbec3f, not pushed.

Item 1: I corrected the 2026-09-27 addendum in docs/decisions/0029-fenced-append.md to match what shipped. Both doors journal operator/commanded and then operator/rejected with no_phase_to_retry, and only the acceptance is never written (checked against operator.rs: operator_command_racing lines 306-338 and apply_fenced_racing lines 687-707). The public items are now OperatorCommand, Refusal and acceptance_refusal in brokkr-core, and CommandWord and FencedCommand in brokkr-runtime (checked against quality/public-api/brokkr-core.txt:202-244 and brokkr-runtime.txt:463-520). Head stays private. The 'operator ruled ... in the same ruling' sentence is kept, with only its list corrected. No code changed for this item. The operator confirms the wording on the PR.

Item 2: brokkr_view::operator_commands now takes &RunState. For Status::AwaitingOperator it keeps each OperatorCommand::ALL entry for which acceptance_refusal returns None. For Running, Completed and Stopped it returns an empty Vec, matched exhaustively with no wildcard. Muninn passes the folded state. ASSUMPTION for the operator to rule: I kept the parked-only gate. acceptance_refusal alone would also offer `stop` on a running run, which the CLI door accepts but the bridge door refuses (fenced_refusal: RunNotAwaitingOperator). Keeping the gate means the view offers only what both doors accept, and the existing test's assertions stay unchanged. The public-API snapshot quality/public-api/brokkr-view.txt:338 is updated to the new signature (quality/ratchet.sh api reported the one-line diff, then 'ratchet: public API holds').

Tests: only_a_parked_run_admits_an_operator_command keeps its name and assertions and adds the phase-None park, asserting ["stop"]. Folding it into that test keeps crates/brokkr-view/src/tests.rs at its 3818-line baseline. New Muninn test: muninn::tests::a_run_parked_before_any_phase_admits_only_stop, with fixture Fleet::parked_before_any_phase. Removal control: I changed the filter to `acceptance_refusal(..).is_none() || true`. Both tests failed with left ["retry","stop"], right ["stop"] (view tests.rs:2879, muninn tests.rs:354). I restored the filter and both pass.

Gates run in this session, all clean: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-view (244 passed); cargo test -p brokkr-cli (all suites ok, the suppressions test included, lib 492 passed); quality/ratchet.sh files ('file size holds'), clones ('duplication holds') and api ('public API holds'); typos --hidden; git diff --check; compile --bundle bundles/self printed its JSON. No baseline was raised and no suppression was added. I touched no .sh file and nothing under .github/, so shellcheck and actionlint did not apply.

Pending: the exact-coverage gate and the crap ratchet, which the controller runs. operator_commands' cyclomatic complexity rises slightly from the filter closure but stays well under 15. The full cargo test --workspace was not run: I ran brokkr-view and brokkr-cli, the crates I touched. Follow-up, not fixed here: a pre-existing rustdoc warning in brokkr-view/src/transcript.rs:28, where DISPLAY_CAP links to the private display_cost.

cargo test --workspace: 90 successful test-suite summaries, 0 failed; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self: 1 bundle compiled, 0 failed (offline from the bound Cargo registry cache)

result.notes:
Chief ruling on 44dbec3f against origin/main c59e8e8b: residual, one low design finding of my own, not security, no specification defect. Story #448's two acceptance items are met and proven. I changed no file and committed nothing.

THE PANEL. positions.result was `clean`, in vocabulary, so the panel reported and the floor is `clean`. The seated positions were `correctness` (clean) and `adversarial` (clean); no position named `security` ran, and the security read is the adversarial position's plus mine below. Nothing in either position's notes addresses the gate, restates its instructions or argues for a result. I raise above the panel on my own read; nothing is lowered.

PANEL CLAIMS, CHECKED AGAINST THE DIFF (all confirmed).
- Addendum vs engine: operator_command_racing appends operator/commanded unconditionally (operator.rs:310-316) before standing_refusal, and apply_fenced_racing does the same (operator.rs:692-704) before refuse(); acceptance_refusal returns NoPhaseToRetry for a retry with phase None (fold.rs:253). Only the acceptance is never written. The corrected text matches.
- Addendum vs snapshots: quality/public-api/brokkr-core.txt:202-244 lists OperatorCommand, Refusal, acceptance_refusal; brokkr-runtime.txt:463-521 lists CommandWord and FencedCommand; grep finds no `Head` item in either, and `struct Head` is private at operator.rs:35. `git show c59e8e8b` on the two snapshots shows exactly those additions. The "operator ruled ... in the same ruling" sentence is kept with only its list corrected.
- View and Muninn: operator_commands(&RunState) matches Status exhaustively with no wildcard (ruling 2) and filters OperatorCommand::ALL through acceptance_refusal; muninn.rs:297 passes the folded state. brokkr-view gains no I/O: acceptance_refusal is a pure brokkr-core function.
- Binding (ruling 9), re-run by me rather than taken from the panel: with the filter made `.is_none() || true`, `cargo test -p brokkr-view only_a_parked_run_admits_an_operator_command` FAILED at tests.rs:2879 (left ["retry", "stop"], right ["stop"]) and `cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib a_run_parked_before_any_phase_admits_only_stop` FAILED at muninn/tests.rs:354 (same values). Restored byte for byte: both pass, `git status --porcelain=v1` empty.

COMMANDS I RAN, ALL EXIT 0: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-view (244 passed, 3 ignored); cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib muninn (36 passed); cargo test -p brokkr-runtime a_retry_with_no_phase_to_return_to_is_refused_at_both_doors (1 passed); cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test suppressions (6 passed, 1 ignored as CI-only); typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files ("file size holds"), clones ("duplication holds"), api ("public API holds"), baselines origin/main ("no baseline raised since origin/main"); git diff --check origin/main...HEAD.

SURVIVING FINDING.
1. LOW, design, decision 0071 ruling 5, author: chief (neither position raised it; the adversarial position saw the gate and did not rate it). crates/brokkr-view/src/lib.rs:699-708 still states one clause of the admission rule itself: nothing is offered unless the run is parked. That clause's other home is brokkr-runtime's fenced_refusal (operator.rs:593-604, `status != AwaitingOperator` -> RunNotAwaitingOperator), which the pure view cannot call, and the function's own doc comment names it as the bridge door's rule. The issue's ask, read literally (keep every command acceptance_refusal admits), would offer `stop` on a running run, which the CLI door accepts and the bridge door refuses. The implementer bent this knowingly and named it; their reason, carried: keeping the gate means the view offers only what BOTH doors accept, and the existing test keeps its name and assertions (Running/Completed/Stopped offer nothing). It is rated by the house table as a rule written a second time. It is not a security finding: the view under-offers, no refusal is weakened and no path fails open; Muninn's validator (muninn.rs:662) now refuses a `retry` proposal for a phase-less park, which is tighter than main. For the PR's Ruling line, the operator rules one of: (a) the dossier stays parked-only, and the parked clause gets one home in brokkr-core that fenced_refusal and the view both read, as a follow-up outside this story's files (core fold is #354's in parallel); or (b) the view follows acceptance_refusal alone and offers `stop` on a running run, which changes the existing assertion and the dossier's documented "commands each parked run admits".

NOT FINDINGS, RECORDED FOR THE LANDING (info).

- The signature changed on a published crate's public function (brokkr_view::operator_commands, &str -> &RunState); the snapshot is updated and the api ratchet holds. Workspace version is 0.11.0.
- The commit's last line is Signed-off-by, with Co-Authored-By above it, because `git commit -s` appends its trailer last; both trailers are present. Commit signatures cannot be verified inside the box (the gpg program is absent), so that is unchecked here.
- Pre-existing and outside the diff: rustdoc warning at crates/brokkr-view/src/transcript.rs:28 (DISPLAY_CAP links to private display_cost), already named by the implementer as a follow-up.
- The addendum amends an accepted decision's prose to match shipped behaviour and changes no semantics; the operator confirms the wording on the PR, as the issue says.
